subject: botany
question_text: Write a note on the economic importance of algae and bryophytes.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book pp.8-9, SAQ 5 (the algae half ends p.8; the bryophyte half opens p.9). The book lists four algae points (food, agar, iodine, SCP) and two bryophyte points (Sphagnum peat, succession); the card adds NCERT's CO2-fixation, hydrocolloid, erosion-control and animal-food points. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The 2+2 split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Economic importance of algae
lines: Algae carry out about half of the total
carbon dioxide fixation on earth by
photosynthesis (primary producers).
Food: species of Porphyra, Laminaria and
Sargassum are eaten.
Agar, from Gelidium and Gracilaria, is
used in microbiological media and in
ice-creams and jellies.
Chlorella and Spirulina are used as
single-cell protein (SCP).
steps.why: Two marks here mean about four correct uses with named organisms. NCERT's list: half of all CO₂ fixation, food species, agar, hydrocolloids (algin from brown algae, carrageen from red) and SCP; the book also notes iodine extracted from Laminaria.
common_mistakes: Naming uses without the organisms — 'agar from Gelidium' earns; bare 'agar' may not.
Writing 'sea grasses' as the food — the food algae are Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum.
steps.memory_tip: Five uses in one line: air (CO₂ fixation), food, agar, gels (algin, carrageen), protein (SCP).
steps.margin_note: About four points with named genera fill the two marks.

steps.label: Economic importance of bryophytes

lines.text: Main uses: Sphagnum peat + role in succession

lines: Sphagnum provides peat, used as fuel and
as packing material for trans-shipment
of living material (it holds water).
Mosses with lichens are the first
colonisers of bare rocks (plant
succession).
Moss carpets reduce the impact of falling
rain and prevent soil erosion.
Some mosses are food for herbaceous
mammals and birds.
steps.why: Bryophytes matter less commercially but greatly ecologically: Sphagnum peat is the one economic product, while succession, erosion control and animal food are the ecological uses. The book lists only peat and succession; NCERT adds the erosion and food points.
common_mistakes: Writing that Sphagnum gives agar — agar comes from red algae; Sphagnum gives peat.
Leaving out why Sphagnum packs living material — its water-holding capacity is the reason.
steps.memory_tip: One product, three services: peat, then succession, erosion control and food for animals.
steps.margin_note: Two or three bryophyte points with Sphagnum named fill these two marks.

insider_note: Split the answer visibly into 'Algae:' and 'Bryophytes:' halves — examiners award two marks per labelled half.
